name: Cold Brew
steps: Put coarsely ground coffee in a clean jar large enough for the measured cold drinking water. Fine grounds make filtering slower and can leave sediment.
Pour in the water gradually and stir until all grounds are wet, with no dry pockets floating on top. Cover the jar.
Refrigerate for 12–18 hours; this steeping time is additional to the listed active time. A longer steep within this range generally gives a stronger flavour.
Set a coffee filter over a clean receiving jug and strain slowly. Let the liquid drip through naturally without squeezing the grounds, which can force sediment into the drink.
Taste a small amount and dilute with drinking water or milk if desired. Serve chilled and keep any remainder covered in the refrigerator.
tips: Use coarse grounds and filter thoroughly.
substitutions: Any substitution changes the recipe: recheck allergies, Jain rules and quantities.
passiveTime: Allow additional soaking, resting, chilling or fermentation as specified in the steps.
notes: Prices are sample ingredient-cost assumptions. Replace with supplier rates before procurement.
